- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0.0) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overestimates continuation — cap next 3–5 day forecast at +2–3% above true peak.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg 0.0–0.3), model frequently underestimates downward moves — add 1–3% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 1–3 days — if true price is trending down from 3–5 day avg, forecast should be adjusted down 1–2% per day for next 3 days.  
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0.3), model often overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1–2% below 30-day moving average of true prices.  
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.5), model exhibits high variance — use 30-day true price median as anchor, adjust forecast ±1–2% based on sentiment direction.
